highlights: 今日技术圈焦点集中在 OpenAI 的产品迭代与巨头博弈上，新版 ChatGPT 超级应用因界面混乱引发用户体验争议，促使官方紧急澄清功能边界与升级机制。同时，OpenAI 与苹果之间的人才争夺战愈演愈烈，苹果对前者激进挖角其硬件与设计高管的行为表达了强烈不满。在开发者生态与复古计算领域，sqlite-utils 迎来小版本更新，而原生支持现代 macOS 的 HyperCard 播放器则唤起了技术圈的怀旧情怀。此外，素数猜想的数学进展与科技记者的纪念文章，也为硬核技术之外增添了人文与科学的多元色彩。

articles.title: Benedict Evans on the New ‘Super App’ ChatGPT
articles.titleZh: Benedict Evans 评全新 ChatGPT“超级应用”
articles.summary: 新版 ChatGPT“超级应用”的用户体验遭到知名分析师 Benedict Evans 的严厉批评。他指出该应用界面混乱，项目、任务和聊天之间的界限模糊不清。此外，聊天窗口采用糟糕的浮动设计，而插件选项却显示为模板，且强制要求绑定 Slack 或 Google Drive 才能完成设置。这反映了在主导型公司中，产品功能堆砌往往导致交互逻辑的割裂。
articles.summaryEn: The new ChatGPT "super app" faces severe criticism from analyst Benedict Evans for its chaotic user experience. He points out the blurred boundaries between projects, tasks, and chats, making navigation confusing. Furthermore, the UI is inconsistent with floating chat windows, misleading "plugins" labeled as "templates," and a forced setup requiring Slack or Google Drive. This highlights how feature accumulation in dominant companies often leads to fragmented interaction logic.
articles.reason: 了解行业顶尖分析师对 OpenAI 新版 ChatGPT 应用设计缺陷的直击痛点的批评。

articles.title: sqlite-utils 4.1
articles.summary: sqlite-utils 发布了 4.0 版本后的首个小版本更新 4.1，引入了多项次要新功能。其中，`sqlite-utils insert` 和 `sqlite-utils upsert` 命令现在支持 `--code` 选项，允许在插入或更新数据时执行 Python 代码进行转换。该版本进一步完善了命令行工具的数据处理能力，为开发者提供了更灵活的数据库操作方式。
articles.summaryEn: sqlite-utils has released version 4.1, the first minor update since 4.0, introducing several minor new features. Notably, the `sqlite-utils insert` and `sqlite-utils upsert` commands now support a `--code` option, allowing Python code execution for data transformation during insertion or updates. This version further enhances the CLI's data processing capabilities, offering developers more flexible database operations.
articles.reason: 快速了解 sqlite-utils 4.1 版本中新增的 `--code` 选项等实用功能。

blocks.text: The first dot-release since 4.0 a few days ago, introducing a number of minor new features.

sqlite-utils insert and sqlite-utils upsert now accept a --code option for providing a block of Python code (or a path to a .py file) that defines a rows() function or rows iterable of rows to insert, as an alternative to importing from a file. (#684)
sqlite-utils already had features that allow you to pass blocks of Python code as CLI arguments, for example this one for the sqlite-utils convert command:
Allowing blocks of code to generate new rows directly was on obvious extension of that pattern:

sqlite-utils insert and sqlite-utils upsert now accept --type column-name type to override the type automatically chosen when the table is created. This is useful for CSV or TSV columns such as ZIP codes that look like integers but should be stored as TEXT to preserve leading zeros. (#131)
A long-standing feature request which turned out to be a simple implementation.

New table.drop_index(name) method and sqlite-utils drop-index command for dropping an index by name. Both accept ignore=True/--ignore to ignore a missing index. (#626)
sqlite-utils query can now read the SQL query from standard input by passing - in place of the query, for example echo "select * from dogs" | sqlite-utils query dogs.db -. (#765)
Two more small features. I had Codex review all open issues and highlight the easiest ones!
sqlite-utils upsert can now infer the primary key of an existing table, so --pk can be omitted when upserting into a table that already has a primary key.
Another Codex suggestion, an obvious missing CLI feature from a Python library improvement that shipped in the 4.0 release.

table.transform() and table.transform_sql() now accept strict=True or strict=False to change a table’s SQLite strict mode. Omitting the option preserves the existing mode. (#787)
The sqlite-utils transform command now accepts --strict and --no-strict to change a table’s strict mode. (#787)
These two were inspired by Prefer STRICT tables in SQLite by Evan Hahn, which did the rounds on Hacker News today. Evan pointed out that:
Unfortunately, I don’t think there’s a way to ALTER a table to make it strict. I think you have to copy the data out of the non-strict table into the strict one.
That's exactly what the sqlite-utils transform mechanism does, so I extended it to add the ability to switch tables from strict to non-strict and vice-versa.
Here's the GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh Codex transcript I used to implement those new strict table features. One of the most useful prompts I ran was this one:
use uv run python -c and manually exercise the new .transform(strict=) option, see if you can find any edge-cases or bugs
Effectively telling the model to manually test its work, outside of the automated tests it had already written. This turned up two minor issues that we then fixed.

translations: 这是几天前发布 4.0 版本以来的第一个小版本更新，引入了一些次要的新功能。
sqlite-utils insert 和 sqlite-utils upsert 现在接受 --code 选项，用于提供一段 Python 代码（或 .py 文件路径），该代码定义了要插入的 rows() 函数或 rows 可迭代对象，作为从文件导入的替代方案。(#684)
sqlite-utils 已经具备允许将 Python 代码块作为 CLI 参数传递的功能，例如 sqlite-utils convert 命令的这个功能：
允许代码块直接生成新行是该模式的一个明显扩展：
sqlite-utils insert 和 sqlite-utils upsert 现在接受 --type column-name type 参数，以覆盖创建表时自动选择的类型。这对于 CSV 或 TSV 列（例如邮政编码）非常有用，它们看起来像整数，但应存储为 TEXT 以保留前导零。(#131)
这是一个长期以来的功能请求，结果证明实现起来非常简单。

新增 table.drop_index(name) 方法和 sqlite-utils drop-index 命令，用于按名称删除索引。两者都接受 ignore=True/--ignore 以忽略缺失的索引。(#626) sqlite-utils query 现在可以通过传递 - 代替查询语句来从标准输入读取 SQL 查询，例如 echo "select * from dogs" | sqlite-utils query dogs.db -。(#765)
还有两个小功能。我让 Codex 审查了所有未解决的问题，并突出了最容易解决的问题！
sqlite-utils upsert 现在可以推断现有表的主键，因此在向已有主键的表进行 upsert 操作时可以省略 --pk。
这是 Codex 的另一个建议，是 4.0 版本中发布的 Python 库改进中明显缺失的一个 CLI 功能。
table.transform() 和 table.transform_sql() 现在接受 strict=True 或 strict=False 来更改表的 SQLite 严格模式。省略该选项将保留现有模式。(#787) sqlite-utils transform 命令现在接受 --strict 和 --no-strict 来更改表的严格模式。(#787)
这两个功能是受 Evan Hahn 的《Prefer STRICT tables in SQLite》一文启发，该文今天在 Hacker News 上广为流传。Evan 指出：
遗憾的是，我认为没有办法通过 ALTER 将表变为严格模式。我认为你必须将数据从非严格表复制到严格表中。
这正是 sqlite-utils transform 机制所做的事情，因此我对其进行了扩展，增加了在严格表和非严格表之间切换的功能。
这是我用来实现这些新严格表功能的 GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh Codex 记录。我运行过的最有用的提示词之一是这个：
使用 uv run python -c 手动测试新的 .transform(strict=) 选项，看看能否发现任何边缘情况或错误
这实际上是让模型在它已经编写的自动化测试之外，手动测试其工作。这发现了两个小问题，随后我们进行了修复。

articles.title: Gurman on Tang Tan and Paul Meade
articles.titleZh: Gurman 谈 Tang Tan 与 Paul Meade 的人才争夺战
articles.summary: 彭博社记者 Mark Gurman 报道了苹果对 OpenAI 激进挖角行为的警惕与不满。OpenAI 近期持续挖走苹果的硬件和设计高管，甚至在今年 6 月挖走了苹果智能眼镜项目负责人 Paul Meade。苹果对此反应强烈，直接让 Meade 离职且未提供过渡期。这标志着两家科技巨头在硬件人才争夺上的冲突正在升级。
articles.summaryEn: Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reports on Apple's alarm and dissatisfaction regarding OpenAI's aggressive poaching. OpenAI has recently been luring away Apple's senior hardware and design leaders, including smart glasses chief Paul Meade in June. Apple reacted strongly by immediately showing Meade the door without offering a transition period. This marks an escalating conflict between the two tech giants in the battle for hardware talent.
articles.reason: 洞察 OpenAI 与苹果之间围绕硬件核心人才日益激烈的争夺内幕。

articles.title: OpenAI Help Center Describes What Is Wrong With the New ChatGPT
articles.titleZh: OpenAI 帮助中心解释新版 ChatGPT 的问题
articles.summary: OpenAI 帮助中心发文澄清了新版 ChatGPT 中 Work 和 Codex 功能的可用范围与运行机制。Work 功能面向符合条件的付费用户，支持在网页端、移动端和桌面应用中使用。网页和移动端的 Work 在云端运行，而桌面端 Work 可以在授权后访问本地文件和应用，但云端与桌面端的对话数据目前并不互通。Codex 功能也在此文中明确了其使用场景。
articles.summaryEn: OpenAI's Help Center has published an article clarifying the availability and operational mechanics of the Work and Codex features in the new ChatGPT. The Work feature is available to eligible paid users across web, mobile, and desktop apps. Work on web and mobile runs in the cloud, while the desktop version can access local files and apps with permission, though cloud and desktop conversations currently do not sync. The usage scenarios for the Codex feature are also specified in the article.
articles.reason: 搞清楚新版 ChatGPT 中 Work 与 Codex 功能在不同平台上的具体差异和数据同步逻辑。

articles.title: Can Someone Explain to Me How to Get ‘ChatGPT Classic’?
articles.titleZh: 谁能解释一下如何获取“ChatGPT Classic”？
articles.summary: OpenAI 帮助中心说明了从旧版 Mac 应用升级到全新“超级应用”版本的具体步骤。用户下载新应用并登录同一账号后，新版应用可能会与旧版并存安装。新版 ChatGPT 集成了 Chat、Work 和 Codex 功能，而旧版则被重命名为“ChatGPT Classic”。用户无需强制迁移，可继续使用旧版应用。
articles.summaryEn: OpenAI's Help Center explains the specific steps to upgrade from the old Mac app to the new "super app" version. After downloading the new app and signing in with the same account, the new version may install alongside the old one. The new ChatGPT integrates Chat, Work, and Codex features, while the previous app is renamed "ChatGPT Classic." Users are not forced to migrate and can continue using the classic version.
articles.reason: 了解新旧版 ChatGPT 桌面应用并存机制及“ChatGPT Classic”的由来。

articles.title: Stacks — HyperCard Player for Modern MacOS
articles.titleZh: Stacks — 现代 MacOS 上的 HyperCard 播放器
articles.summary: Stacks 是一款专为现代 macOS 打造的原生应用，允许用户无需模拟器即可直接运行经典的 HyperCard 堆栈。该应用支持一键浏览并运行互联网档案馆中的 HyperCard 收藏，完美还原了那个时代的排版、音效和 MacinTalk 语音合成功能。它不仅具备跨堆栈导航能力，还在视觉和体验上精准复刻了 1987 年的 Mac 风格，同时保持了现代 Mac 应用的精致感。
articles.summaryEn: Stacks is a native app built for modern macOS, allowing users to run classic HyperCard stacks directly without an emulator. The app supports one-click browsing and running of the Internet Archive's HyperCard collection, perfectly recreating the era's typography, sound effects, and MacinTalk speech synthesis. It offers cross-stack navigation and accurately replicates the 1987 Mac style in both visuals and experience, while maintaining the refinement of a modern Mac app.
articles.reason: 体验一款将复古计算与现代 macOS 原生设计完美融合的 HyperCard 播放器。

articles.title: Progress on Gilbreath’s conjecture
articles.summary: Gilbreath 猜想是一个关于素数的简单却奇特的数学猜想，普通人也能理解其基本逻辑。著名数学家保罗·埃尔德什曾推测该猜想是正确的，但至今仍未得到严格证明。文章回顾了该猜想的历史背景，并探讨了近期在相关领域取得的研究进展。这展示了即使是看似简单的数论问题，也可能蕴含着极深的数学难度。
articles.summaryEn: Gilbreath's conjecture is a simple yet bizarre mathematical conjecture about prime numbers that anyone can understand. The famous mathematician Paul Erdős once speculated that the conjecture is true, but it remains unproven to this day. The article reviews the historical background of the conjecture and explores recent research progress in the field. This demonstrates that even seemingly simple number theory problems can harbor profound mathematical difficulties.
articles.reason: 跟进一个连埃尔德什都关注、简单易懂却至今未解的素数猜想的最新研究动态。

fullText.siteName: John D. Cook | Applied Mathematics Consulting

blocks.text: Years ago I wrote about Gilbreath’s conjecture. It’s a simple conjecture; you could explain it to anyone who understands what prime numbers are. See the linked post for a description of the problem.
Gilbreath’s conjecture is simple, but it’s also kinda weird. As I wrote before,
Paul Erdős speculated that Gilbreath’s conjecture is true but it would be 200 years before anyone could prove it. I find Erdős’s conjecture more interesting than Gilbreath’s conjecture.

The conjecture is hard in a way that, say, solving a nasty-looking differential equation is not. Over the last three centuries, mathematics has developed quite a toolbox for solving differential equations. But Gilbreath’s conjecture is just odd enough that it’s not at all what kind of tool might be useful in approaching it.

Terence Tao has a new blog post announcing a paper that he and two coauthors wrote on a random model intended to mimic Gilbreath’s calculation on primes. This random model is more sophisticated than the little game Gilbreath was playing, but it’s also much more amenable to analysis by established techniques. Tao’s post gives a heuristic explanation for why Gilbreath’s conjecture is plausible, but then adds
However, it seems well beyond current technology to try to make these heuristics rigorous; even the first step … is far out of reach.
Related posts
Moessner’s Magic
Closed form solutions to PDEs

articles.title: ★ Exactly Like Om Malik
articles.titleZh: 宛如 Om Malik 本人
articles.summary: 本文是一篇针对知名科技记者 Om Malik 的纪念文章合集，汇集了各界对他的追忆、致敬与相关故事。文章通过多视角的回忆，展现了 Om Malik 在科技新闻界的深远影响及其个人魅力。这些文字不仅是对他职业生涯的总结，也反映了他在同行和读者心中留下的独特印记。
articles.summaryEn: This article is a collection of memorial pieces for the renowned tech journalist Om Malik, gathering remembrances, tributes, and stories from various circles. Through multi-perspective recollections, the article showcases Om Malik's profound influence in the tech journalism world and his personal charisma. These words are not only a summary of his career but also reflect the unique mark he left on his peers and readers.
articles.reason: 通过同行与朋友的追忆，了解科技新闻界传奇人物 Om Malik 的影响力与个人魅力。

blocks.text: Fred Vogelstein (Om’s partner at Crazy Stupid Tech):

We met a week later at his outdoor office — a bench in SF’s South
Park. He told me that he was going emeritus at True Ventures, the
VC firm, and that he was going to spend more of his time writing.

It was awesome to see him. Sitting on a bench with Om could be
quasi religious. He talked so softly and deliberately that it
forced you to slow down, lean in and forget about everything else.

What became clear was that we actually saw the world the same
way. We didn’t agree what Wired should be doing about it. But
we did agree on this: While everyone was fixated on big tech,
an explosion in tech innovation not seen in a generation was
taking place. We both agreed that not enough people were
writing about it.

“Maybe we should do something together then,” I said.
Joanna Stern:

So saddened to hear about @om. His writing was one of the
reasons I went into tech journalism. Right out of college, I was
working at a PR agency and started reading his site. It inspired
me to start blogging.

Years later, he tried to recruit me. Even after I went elsewhere,
he’d send me notes telling me how proud he was of my work. He’d
often review my reviews, so here’s mine of him: Generous with his
time. Honest with his feedback. Endlessly encouraging to those
coming up behind him.
Casey Newton:

Very sad to hear about the passing of @om. He shared two lasting
lessons with me: the first when I was a cub tech reporter at the
SF Chronicle; he interviewed me for a job but told me he didn’t
think I could hack it at GigaOm because newspaper writers were too
slow. It taught me that I needed to get out of print media ASAP.

The second was many years later, when I was having a drink with
him and some other reporters. We asked him for advice. “Never name
a blog after yourself,” he said. RIP
Jim Nielsen:

One day on Twitter I got a DM from someone with the handle @om.

“I don’t know who this is,” I thought, “but damn that is a great
handle!”

Then I peaked at the follower count: over 1 million!

“WTF? Who is this???” I thought.

I’d never — then or since — been contacted by someone with such
a high profile online.

How was I even on this person’s radar?
Om seemingly read everything.
Jason Hiner, in a post on LinkedIn:

This is the opening anecdote from “Chapter Six: The Blogger” from
my 2016 book, Follow the Geeks, co-authored with Lyndsey Gilpin.
Om once told me that “For three years, it was every day a
rejection” as he tried to break into tech journalism. This was how
he finally broke through.

David Churbuck checked his voicemail. There was a message from
someone looking for a job.

Because of the guy’s thick Indian accent, David could barely make
out what he was saying, except that he worked for a wire service
down on Wall Street and was a big Forbes fan. The guy heard that
Forbes was going to be one of the first media companies to launch
its magazine on the web and he wanted to come help.

David ignored the message. He had a small team and hardly
any budget.

Then he got a fax. It was from this guy, explaining why he was a
perfect fit to join the team.

The next day, the guy left another message. If David would just
give him a call, it would be great to talk with him. He wouldn’t
regret it.

Ignore.

The following day, he left another. Whatever time limit there was
for voicemails, this guy always used up every minute.

Still, David ignored it.

And then the guy started getting creative.

[...]

One of the journalists, Michael Noer, said half jokingly, “Just
call the guy in!” So, partly out of admiration, and partly out of
pure morbid curiosity, David called him back.

One interview. Fifteen minutes. That was all it took for David to
hire Om Malik.
“They do not sell themselves”, Om told me in a separate story from that same time in his life.
Hiner made the entire chapter available to read as a handsome PDF. It’s so good, and so utterly Om. It’s a crackerjack good read about the very early “WWW” days of the web. A bit:

Om is charming and disarming, forceful and accommodating. He has
an easy smile, a quiet, melodic voice, and a handsome face. Once
he opens his mouth, it’s obvious how much he reads and how thirsty
he is to learn. It’s rare to meet someone who is ready to debate
you on almost any topic, but who’s also genuinely curious about
your life and your opinion. It all makes the burly journalist one
of the most huggable people on Earth. That’s what David was up
against when he met Om. He didn’t stand a chance.

“It was destiny,” said David, with a self-deprecating laugh. “It
was total destiny.”
Om’s close friend, photographer Christopher Michel, published “Om the Great”, an enormous gallery of portraits of him. Here’s just one of hundreds:
Lastly, here’s a story from Andrew Sasaki, which he sent me by email, and I’m reproducing with his permission. It’s the perfect Om story:

I met Om briefly at a tech event in NYC around 2008 or so. He was
talking with a friend of mine, and when I walked up he introduced
himself: “Hi, I’m Om.”

“‘Om’ like ‘Om Malik’?” I asked.

This amused him greatly.

“Yes, exactly like Om Malik”, he said.

A couple of years later the iPad had just launched, and I saw my
friend again at another industry event. I asked him a question
related to the unprecedented development effort we were already
seeing around the new platform that didn’t yet have a single
compelling use case.

“You know who I bet would know about that? Om Malik”, he said, and
gave me Om’s email address.

I hesitated to bother Om, but eventually reached out with my
question. “I don’t know if you remember me, but we met a couple of
years ago, and…” blah blah blah.

Naturally, there was no answer. Why would there be? He doesn’t
know me from Adam, and he’s Om Fucking Malik.

Except there was an answer about 4 days later. Om started off by
apologizing for the delay in responding, but he had taken the time
to research his answer before writing to me. And of course, his
answer was thoughtful, insightful, and absolutely correct. I was
gobsmacked at the generosity he had shown replying to someone he
didn’t even know. He gave no indication that he even remembered me
until his signature line:

“Exactly Like Om Malik”

translations: 弗雷德·沃格斯坦（Om 在 Crazy Stupid Tech 的合伙人）：

一周后，我们在他的露天办公室——旧金山 South Park 的一张长椅上见了面。他告诉我，他将在风险投资公司 True Ventures 转为名誉合伙人，并打算把更多时间花在写作上。见到他真是太棒了。和 Om 坐在长椅上简直有一种近乎宗教般的体验。他说话轻柔而从容，让你不得不放慢节奏，倾身细听，忘却周遭的一切。显而易见的是，我们看待世界的方式其实是一致的。我们在 Wired 应该如何应对方面存在分歧，但在这一点上我们达成了共识：当所有人都盯着大型科技公司时，一场一代人未曾见过的科技创新大爆发正在发生。我们都认为，关于这一点写的人还不够多。“也许我们应该一起做点什么，”我说。
乔安娜·斯特恩：
听到关于 @om 的消息非常难过。他的文章是我进入科技新闻行业的原因之一。刚大学毕业时，我在一家 PR 机构工作，开始阅读他的网站。这启发了我开始写博客。几年后，他试图招募我。即使后来我去了别处，他也会发信息告诉我他为我的工作感到多么骄傲。他经常点评我的评论，所以这里是我对他的评价：慷慨付出时间。坦诚给予反馈。对后辈给予无尽的鼓励。
凯西·牛顿：
听到 @om 去世的消息非常难过。他给我留下了两个难忘的教训：第一个是在我还是《旧金山纪事报》（SF Chronicle）的一名新手科技记者时；他面试了我，但告诉我他认为我在 GigaOm 撑不下来，因为报纸记者太慢了。这让我明白我需要尽快离开纸媒。第二个是在多年以后，我和他以及其他几名记者一起喝酒时。我们向他寻求建议。“永远不要用你自己的名字给博客命名，”他说。 RIP
吉姆·尼尔森：
有一天在 Twitter 上，我收到了一个账号名为 @om 的人发来的 DM。“我不知道这是谁，”我心想，“但这名字真棒！”然后我瞥了一眼他的粉丝数：超过 100 万！“WTF？这人是谁？？？”我心想。我以前从未——无论当时还是现在——被网络上如此高调的人联系过。我怎么会进入这个人的视线？
Om 似乎什么都读。
杰森·海纳（Jason Hiner）在 LinkedIn 的一篇帖子中写道：

这是我2016年与Lyndsey Gilpin合著的书《Follow the Geeks》中“第六章：博主”的开篇轶事。Om曾告诉我，在他试图进入科技新闻界时，“整整三年，每天都在被拒绝”。这就是他最终取得突破的方式。David Churbuck查看了他的语音信箱。有一条来自某个找工作的人的留言。因为那家伙浓重的印度口音，David几乎听不清他在说什么，只知道他在华尔街的一家通讯社工作，而且是Forbes的超级粉丝。那家伙听说Forbes将成为首批在网络上推出杂志的媒体公司之一，他想来帮忙。David忽略了这条留言。他的团队很小，几乎没有预算。然后他收到了一份传真。是这个家伙发来的，解释了为什么他是加入团队的完美人选。第二天，那家伙又留了一条信息。如果David能给他打个电话，和他聊聊就太好了。他不会后悔的。忽略。第二天，他又留了一条。不管语音信箱的时间限制是多少，这家伙总是用满每一分钟。David还是忽略了它。然后这家伙开始发挥创意。[...] 其中一位记者Michael Noer半开玩笑地说：“干脆把这家伙叫进来吧！”于是，一半出于钦佩，一半出于纯粹病态的好奇心，David给他回了电话。一次面试。十五分钟。这就是David雇佣Om Malik所需要的一切。
“他们不会推销自己”，Om在讲述他生命中同一时期的另一个故事时告诉我。
Hiner将整章内容制作成精美的PDF供人阅读。它太棒了，而且完全是Om的风格。这是一篇关于早期“WWW”网络时代的绝佳读物。一小段：

Om迷人且令人放下戒备，强势又随和。他有着随和的笑容、安静而富有旋律感的声音，以及英俊的面庞。一旦他开口，就能明显看出他读了多少书，以及他对学习的渴望。很难遇到一个人既准备好在几乎任何话题上与你辩论，又对你的生活和观点真正感到好奇。这一切让这位魁梧的记者成为地球上最让人想拥抱的人之一。这就是David遇到Om时所面临的局面。他毫无胜算。“这是命中注定，”David自嘲地笑着说。“完全是命中注定。”
Om的密友、摄影师Christopher Michel发布了《Om the Great》，这是一个包含他大量肖像的画廊。这里只是数百张中的一张：
最后，这是一个来自Andrew Sasaki的故事，他通过电子邮件发给了我，我在征得他同意后在此转载。这是一个完美的关于Om的故事：
“正是 Om Malik”

articles.title: Another Ridiculous Interrail Holiday - 6,379Km and 13 Countries over 7 weeks
articles.titleZh: 又一次疯狂的欧洲火车之旅——7 周跨越 13 国、行驶 6379 公里
articles.summary: 作者分享了与妻子利用欧洲 Interrail 通票进行的第二次长途火车旅行经历。相比去年 30 天游历 10 国的紧凑行程，今年他们选择了“2 个月内 15 个旅行日”的套票，并提前购买了头等舱。整个旅程历时 7 周，跨越 13 个国家，总里程达 6379 公里，期间还包含了两次轮渡体验。这为计划欧洲跨国火车游的旅行者提供了极具参考价值的行程规划与实操经验。
articles.summaryEn: The author shares the experience of a second long-distance train journey across Europe using an Interrail pass with his wife. Compared to last year's intense 30-day, 10-country trip, this year they opted for a "15 travel days in 2 months" package and purchased first-class tickets in advance. The journey lasted 7 weeks, covering 13 countries and a total distance of 6,379 kilometers, including two ferry rides. This provides highly valuable itinerary planning and practical experience for travelers planning a European cross-country train tour.
articles.reason: 获取一份真实且详尽的欧洲 Interrail 头等舱长途火车游行程规划参考。

blocks.text: Last year, my wife and I went on a 5,025 Km Interrail adventure. We got the month-long unlimited pass and saw 10 Countries in 30 Days. That was a bit too intense. So this year we got the 15 travel days in 2 months package. We grabbed the 1st class tickets when they went on sale in December.
Here's how our journey ended up:
The trip included two ferries - one overnight - which had a small Interrail discount. In total we spent approximately 40 hours on trains over a 7 week trip.

This blog post looks at the practicalities of the journey and the experience we had while travelling. You are free to decide which cities you want to visit and which you want to skip. This worked (mostly) for us - you should write a blog post about your own experiences.
London To Brussels
Eurostar St Pancras is dangerously crowded and needs tearing down. You can use RealTimeTrains to see your departure platform before it is announced - that's useful for avoiding some of the queues.

The first-class service in Eurostar is lovely (even if it doesn't get you access to the lounge). Unfortunately, you need to book vegan meals a few days in advance - a deadline I missed. The veggie option was fine though.
Made it to Brussels where we hit our first snag.
Brussels to Hamburg
We'd booked some of our tickets months in advance. What we hadn't realised is that construction work had been announced and our train would be getting is much later than we anticipated.

Neither Interrail (who we booked the seat reservations through) nor DB (who had our contact details) thought to tell us about the change in journey. Nevertheless, we jumped on a train and had a pleasant enough trip up to Germany.

The Interrail refund form is ridiculously complicated and asks for various screenshots. There really ought to be a big "DB Screwed Up" button for an instant refund. Still, after a couple of days the refund came through.
Hamburg to Copenhagen

There's a DB lounge at the station. We received suspicious stares at our Interrail passes which then necessitated deep examination of our seat reservation by two people. Begrudgingly they let us in. There were comfortable seats and some free drinks. It was mostly quiet until various children started crying.
The train was gentle and slow. 1st class got a snack included - veggie but not vegan. For the first time since leaving the UK there were passport checks which were friendly.

At one point there was a quiet announcement in German. We didn't think much of it until everyone started getting off the train. Turns out one of the carriages had suffered a failure and we were turfed out at Nyborg. Approximately 1,000 passengers attempted to board the next available train - it looked like an utter crush. So we waited for the one after that.
We were treated to a train with spectacular panoramic windows as it went over The Bridge.
A friendly guard told us where to change. Arrived a little late and filled in the Interrail compensation form again.
Copenhagen to Göteborg
The lounge in Copenhagen was basic but fine. A few bowls of fruit and a coffee machine but nothing else. Weirdly no train display.

The train had power sockets on the ceiling - along with headphone jacks! Was a little strange seeing cables dripping down from the ceiling. The 1st class seats were a little roomier than standard, but not much in it. Ticket inspector looked confused at Interrail passes but didn't challenge us.
Göteborg to Oslo
Trains were frequent enough that we didn't bother with advance seat reservations. No 1st class, but the quiet zone was spacious enough. Again, a brief glance at the tickets rather than scanning them.
I was heartily impressed to see snack vending machines on a train! Better than someone pushing a cart through I reckon.
Oslo to Stockholm

There were no signs on seats to say reserved and the service was very full. But we got our seats without a problem. There was free fruit and tea / water in the 1st class carriage. WiFi speeds were excellent.
Stockholm to Helsinki (overnight ferry)
Annoyingly, the ferry terminal is a rather long distance from the nearest tram stop which was a bit of an arse.

The check-in to the ferry warns of extra costs if you have the temerity to use the staffed counters - but the automatic check in wouldn't work with our tickets. They wanted to check that we were eligible for the Interrail discount, so we showed them the app - we didn't have to spend a travel day though. They printed out our tickets and didn't charge us extra.

The boat itself was gorgeous. Obviously not full - many of the bars were empty and the disco was dead - but surprisingly they put on a full song and dance show as entertainment. We'd made reservations at one of the fancy restaurants, which was perfectly nice. It was breathtakingly beautiful outside.
The room was basic, but much easier to sleep in than an overnight train. Unfortunately, I fucked up with the timezones. Stockholm is UTC+1 and Helsinki is at UTC+2. I set my alarm an hour too early!
The breakfast buffet was very well stocked for veggie and vegans. Massive queue before opening but not too crowded.
Helsinki to Tallinn (day ferry)

Terminal was a short walk from the tram. It was spacious and had plenty of seating. Again we couldn't use the automated check in and had to show our Interrail apps. Ferry was small but plenty of room to sit or go shopping.
Tallinn to Riga

Slightly confusing process to buy the tickets as they only went on sale a few weeks before departure. No seat reservations for the first half of the journey - we were slightly worried by the number of people waiting for the three-carriage train. In the end there was plenty of space. Again, 1st class a bit roomier than standard but not dramatically so.
The ticket inspector gave a confused look at the Interrail pass and issued us with a receipt for €0.00!
The train had an onboard ticket vending machine with contactless payments and, delightfully, some bowls of water for dogs.
We changed at Valga which was simple - literally walk across the platform to the waiting train. It was a little more crowded, but plenty of seats.
Riga to Vilnius
1st class was a bit crowded but pleasant until the boomer Brits started ignoring the quiet carriage signs. They were shut up by the guard. Complimentary sparkling water.
Vilnius to Warsaw

There is a VIP lounge in Vilnius - but it is little more than a quiet space with a loo and water fountain. All the snacks and hot drinks were chargeable. We didn't actually have access to it this trip - but the Riga to Vilnius trip did. We scanned our previous ticket reservations to get in.
We weren't able to book seats - because the service said it was sold out. However the train was half empty. No 1st class, but there was WiFi and power, so no complaints from me.
On having our tickets checked we were told that there was 1st class, but we couldn't use it with our Interrail passes. As with most European trains, announcements were in English.

The change at Mockava was easy - we walked to the next platform. We'd booked seats in a little 6 seater cabin - sadly the air con was little more than homeopathic. Even cracking open the window did nothing but waft hot air over us. Fairly full train, toilets were adequate, but the heat was stifling. Even worse, no WiFi!
The train occasionally stopped for several minutes at a time. The crew just opened the doors to let a breeze in - very little health-and-safety culture here!
Mind you, we also saw people crossing the tracks to get to their platform. Yikes!
There were passport checks by armed guards. Brief and inoffensive.
Warsaw to Berlin
Despite the extreme heat, it left on time. This 6 berth 1st class carriage was a bit bigger than the last - and the aircon actually worked.
We were treated to complementary water, juice, and a vegan snack bar! The train driver sounded their horn at every opportunity which wasn't exactly relaxing.
Berlin to München
No vegan currywurst on the DB menu any more 😭.
Annoyingly, we were kicked off at Nuremberg - despite most announcements being made in English this one wasn't, but we figured it out. A train came fairly quickly, so we weren't too late.
München to Verona
There is a 1st class DB lounge but it isn't open to OBB/Interrail scum. Luckily there were plenty of food options for vegans in station. No vegan currywurst on train but several other options.
This was one of two reservations which demanded that it be printed out onto paper and under no circumstances would it be accepted from a screen. That was a lie. Showing the code on-screen was fine.
Verona to Milan

Such a frequent service that no reservations were needed. Annoyingly, the train windows were covered with graffiti so it was impossible to see out. Ticket inspector barely glanced at our tickets. WiFi didn't work. Crowded and a bit noisy. Air con just about coped with the heat.
Milan to Basel

The Interrail app seemed certain that we had to change a dozen times for this journey. Instead, I found a direct train to Olten. The 1st class seats were massive and had a handy compartment for smaller bags. Windows were huge. Again, our passes and reservation were barely glanced at.

As we arrived in Olten there was a train a couple of platforms away which was direct to Basel. Bit of a dash to get it. No 1st class, but it was a double-decker so we got to sit upstairs, which is just as good!
Basel to Paris

The only thing better than 1st class is upstairs on 1st! Big comfy reclining seats. Packed train with not much luggage space. As ever with trains travelling to France, there were warnings about labelling luggage correctly but no one seemed to do it. Zero vegan options on board. C'est la vie!
Paris to London
What a blessing to witness so many people's first ever attempt to queue for a train 🙄

Mad queues to get in to the departure lounge - but the train departed and arrived on time.  I'd remembered to pre-book a vegan option which was tasty and also included a dairy-free chocolate bar. Eurostar's WiFi is shit but 5G worked OK.
What's Next?
Doing Interrail trips like this is brilliant. The trains are usually a lot more relaxing than flying, it's more convenient to arrive in a city centre, and they're less polluting.

Would we do a trip like this again? It's certain a lot of travel. We weren't very spontaneous - most of the trip was planned out way in advance, along with hotels. Having 2-4 days in each place is like taking a series of minibreaks, which is delightful. But it can be exhausting. I don't want to complain that my diamond tiara is too tight, but there comes a point where there is such a thing a too much holiday.

We still have several more European countries to visit; although not all are easy to get to by train. Perhaps we'll fly in somewhere, take the train around, then fly back? Or spend a week only in one country?
If you have tips for further adventures - please let us know!

translations: 去年，我和妻子进行了一次长达5025公里的 Interrail 冒险之旅。我们买了为期一个月的无限次通票，在30天内游历了10个国家。这有点太赶了。所以今年我们买了两个月内可旅行15天的套餐。我们在12月发售时抢到了一等座车票。
以下是我们最终的行程：
这次旅行包括两次渡轮——其中一次是过夜渡轮——享有 Interrail 的一点折扣。在为期7周的旅行中，我们总共在火车上度过了大约40个小时。
这篇博文探讨了旅行的实际操作以及我们在旅途中的体验。你可以自由决定想游览哪些城市以及想跳过哪些。这个行程（大体上）对我们来说是可行的——你也应该写一篇关于你自己经历的博文。
伦敦到布鲁塞尔
欧洲之星（Eurostar）的圣潘克拉斯（St Pancras）车站拥挤得令人担忧，简直需要拆除重建。你可以使用 RealTimeTrains 在官方公布前查看出发站台——这对于避开部分排队队伍很有用。
欧洲之星的一等座服务很棒（即使它不能让你进入贵宾室）。遗憾的是，你需要提前几天预订纯素餐——我错过了这个截止日期。不过，素食选项也还可以。
我们抵达了布鲁塞尔，在那里遇到了第一个小麻烦。
布鲁塞尔到汉堡
我们提前几个月预订了部分车票。我们没有意识到的是，已经公布了施工计划，我们的火车会比预期的晚很多。
无论是 Interrail（我们通过它预订座位）还是 DB（德国铁路公司，拥有我们的联系方式）都没有想到要告诉我们行程的变更。尽管如此，我们还是跳上了一列火车，前往德国的旅途相当愉快。
Interrail 的退款表格复杂得离谱，还要求提供各种截图。真的应该有一个大大的“DB 搞砸了”按钮来提供即时退款。不过，几天后退款还是到账了。
汉堡到哥本哈根
车站里有一个 DB 贵宾室。我们的 Interrail 通票遭到了怀疑的目光，随后需要两个人对我们的座位预订进行深入检查。他们才勉强让我们进去。里面有舒适的座位和一些免费饮料。在几个孩子开始哭闹之前，这里一直很安静。
火车平稳而缓慢。一等座包含一份小吃——是素食但不是纯素。这是离开英国以来第一次进行护照检查，态度很友好。
有一次，广播里用德语做了一个简短的通知。我们没太在意，直到大家开始下车。原来是一节车厢发生了故障，我们在尼堡（Nyborg）被赶下了车。大约1000名乘客试图登上下一班可用的火车——看起来挤得水泄不通。所以我们等了再下一班。
我们乘坐了一列拥有壮观全景车窗的火车，驶过了那座大桥（The Bridge）。
一位友好的列车员告诉我们该在哪里换乘。我们稍微晚点到达，并再次填写了 Interrail 的赔偿表。
哥本哈根到哥德堡
哥本哈根的贵宾室很简陋但还可以。有几碗水果和一台咖啡机，但除此之外什么也没有。奇怪的是，没有列车信息显示屏。
火车的天花板上装有电源插座——还有耳机插孔！看到线缆从天花板上垂下来感觉有点奇怪。一等座的座位比标准座稍微宽敞一点，但差别不大。查票员对 Interrail 通票感到困惑，但没有为难我们。
哥德堡到奥斯陆
火车班次很密，所以我们懒得提前预订座位。没有一等座，但静音车厢足够宽敞。同样，检票只是扫一眼，而不是扫码。
在火车上看到零食自动售货机，真是让我印象深刻！我觉得这比有人推着小车穿过过道要好得多。
奥斯陆到斯德哥尔摩
座位上没有预订标志，而且这趟车非常满。但我们还是顺利找到了座位。一等车厢里有免费的水果、茶和水。WiFi 速度非常快。
斯德哥尔摩到赫尔辛基（夜班渡轮）
令人烦恼的是，渡轮码头离最近的电车站相当远，这有点让人受不了。
渡轮值机处警告说，如果你胆敢使用人工柜台就要收取额外费用——但自动值机机无法处理我们的车票。他们想检查我们是否符合 Interrail 折扣资格，所以我们给他们看了 App——不过我们不需要消耗旅行日。他们打印了我们的票，也没有额外收费。
渡轮本身非常华丽。显然没有满员——许多酒吧都空着，迪斯科舞厅也死气沉沉——但令人惊讶的是，他们安排了一场完整的歌舞表演作为娱乐。我们在一家高档餐厅预订了位置，体验非常棒。外面的景色美得令人窒息。
房间很基础，但比在夜班火车上容易入睡得多。不幸的是，我把时区搞砸了。斯德哥尔摩是 UTC+1，赫尔辛基是 UTC+2。我把闹钟定早了一个小时！
自助早餐为素食主义者和纯素食主义者准备了充足的食物。开门前排了很长的队，但里面并不算太拥挤。
赫尔辛基到塔林（日间渡轮）
从电车站走到码头很近。码头很宽敞，有很多座位。我们还是无法使用自动值机，只能出示我们的 Interrail App。渡轮很小，但有很多空间可以坐下或购物。
塔林到里加
买票的过程有点令人困惑，因为它们在出发前几周才开始发售。前半段旅程没有预订座位——看到那么多人等这趟只有三节车厢的火车，我们有点担心。最后发现空间非常充足。同样，一等座比标准座宽敞一点，但也没有特别夸张。
查票员困惑地看了一眼 Interrail 通票，然后给我们开了一张 0.00 欧元的收据！
火车上有一个支持非接触式支付的自动售票机，而且令人高兴的是，还有几个给狗喝水的水盆。
我们在瓦尔加换乘，非常简单——简直就是走过站台去坐等在那里的火车。车上稍微拥挤了一些，但座位很充足。
里加到维尔纽斯
一等座有点拥挤，但还算舒适，直到那些英国婴儿潮一代开始无视静音车厢的标志。他们被乘务员制止了。提供免费的气泡水。
维尔纽斯到华沙
维尔纽斯有一个 VIP 休息室——但它只不过是一个带有厕所和饮水机的安静空间。所有的零食和热饮都要收费。这次旅行我们其实没有权限进入——但从里加到维尔纽斯的那次是可以进的。我们扫描了之前的订票记录才进去。
我们没能预订到座位——因为系统显示已售罄。然而火车上一半都是空的。没有一等座，但有 WiFi 和电源，所以我没什么可抱怨的。
检票时我们被告知有头等舱，但我们的 Interrail 通票不能使用。和大多数欧洲火车一样，广播使用的是英语。
在 Mockava 换乘很方便——我们走到下一个站台就行了。我们预订了一个 6 人小包厢的座位——遗憾的是，空调形同虚设。即使把窗户开个缝也无济于事，只会把热风吹向我们。火车相当拥挤，厕所还算凑合，但热得让人窒息。更糟的是，没有 WiFi！
火车偶尔会一次停下几分钟。乘务员干脆把门打开让微风吹进来——这里的健康与安全意识非常淡薄！
请注意，我们还看到有人穿过铁轨走到他们的站台。天哪！
有武装警卫进行护照检查。过程简短且没有冒犯之意。
华沙到柏林
尽管天气极其炎热，火车还是准点发车了。这个 6 座头等车厢比上一个稍微大一点——而且空调居然真的能制冷。
我们享用了免费提供的水、果汁和纯素零食棒！火车司机一有机会就按喇叭，这让人实在无法放松。
柏林到慕尼黑
DB 菜单上再也没有纯素咖喱香肠了 😭。
令人恼火的是，我们在纽伦堡被赶下了车——尽管大多数广播都有英语，但这条没有，不过我们还是弄明白了。下一趟火车很快就来了，所以我们也没晚点太多。
慕尼黑到维罗纳
这里有一个 DB 头等舱休息室，但不向 OBB/Interrail 的“底层乘客”开放。幸运的是，车站里有很多纯素食品可供选择。火车上没有纯素咖喱香肠，但还有其他几个选择。
这是两项要求必须打印在纸上、且无论如何不接受屏幕展示的预订之一。那是个谎言。在屏幕上出示代码完全没问题。
维罗纳到米兰
车次非常频繁，不需要预订。令人恼火的是，火车车窗上涂满了涂鸦，根本看不到外面。查票员几乎没怎么看我们的票。WiFi 无法使用。车厢拥挤且有些嘈杂。空调勉强能应付高温。
米兰到巴塞尔
Interrail 应用似乎确信我们这段旅程必须换乘十几次。然而，我找到了一趟直达 Olten 的火车。头等舱的座位非常宽敞，还有一个方便放置小包的隔间。车窗很大。我们的通票和预订再次被草草看了一眼。
当我们到达 Olten 时，隔着几个站台有一趟直达巴塞尔的火车。我们一路狂奔才赶上。虽然没有头等舱，但这是一列双层列车，所以我们坐在了楼上，感觉一样棒！
巴塞尔到巴黎
唯一比头等舱更好的就是头等舱的楼上！宽敞舒适的躺椅。火车挤满了人，行李空间不大。和所有开往法国的火车一样，有警告要求正确标记行李，但似乎没人这么做。车上没有任何纯素选择。这就是生活！
巴黎到伦敦
真是有幸目睹这么多人有生以来第一次尝试排队上火车 🙄
进候车室的队伍排得疯狂——但火车准点出发和到达。我记得提前预订了纯素餐，味道很好，还附带了一块无乳巧克力棒。Eurostar 的 WiFi 糟透了，但 5G 网络还可以。
接下来是什么？
像这样进行 Interrail 旅行真是太棒了。坐火车通常比坐飞机放松得多，到达市中心也更方便，而且污染更少。
我们还会再进行这样的旅行吗？这确实是一趟长途跋涉。我们并没有很随性——大部分行程和酒店都是提前很久规划好的。在每个地方待上2到4天，就像是一连串的短假，令人愉悦。但这也会让人精疲力尽。我不想抱怨我的钻石皇冠太紧，但确实到了某个程度，假期也会显得太多。
我们还有几个欧洲国家要去；尽管并非所有地方都方便乘火车前往。也许我们可以飞到某个地方，然后乘火车四处转转，再飞回来？或者只在一个国家待上一周？
